title: Hazel and the Garden
premise: Hazel Delacroix, youngest keeper of the Ledgermen—a guild that records trades in impossible things—inherits a dying stranger's map and discovers the guild's oldest debt: a king bound body and crown to a devouring thing called the Verdant, which feeds on the memories of the realm. The map leads through the garden where the Verdant was first planted, and Hazel learns his own family's ledgers were the binding's roots, paid for in his grandmother's stolen years. To free the king, Hazel must unbind the garden itself, sacrificing the guild's accumulated memory—including, he believes, his own name—before the last dragon-fire, the only flame that can burn the Verdant's roots, gutters out. In the end Hazel discovers that memory given freely, unlike memory taken, cannot be consumed, and he reforges the guild not as keepers of debts but as keepers of gifts, crowning a king who finally remembers who he is.
about_author: Theo Eriksen is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing estate sales and unclaimed inheritances, an experience that left him convinced every object keeps a grudge. He writes fantasy about paperwork, memory, and the terrible arithmetic of inheritance from a drafty house full of other people's letters.

chapters.title: The Weight of Entries
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the guildhall's cellar, Hazel balances the Ledger of Impossible Things while the last senior members argue over the guild's collapse. A routine entry—a woman trading her shadow for a winter's warmth—establishes the rules of the trade. Emotional beat: quiet pride curdling into dread as Hazel notices entries vanishing from the pages, erased by no hand.

chapters.title: A Stranger at the Ledger Door
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A burned, half-lucid stranger collapses in the guildhall doorway, pressing a map of wax and dragon-scale into Hazel's hands and gasping that the binding is failing. The guild elders refuse the debt, calling it outside their charter. Emotional beat: Hazel's reluctant compassion, and the first thrill of a choice that is truly his.

chapters.title: What the Elders Burned
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with an interlude from the dying stranger. Searching the archives for the map's provenance, Hazel finds a scorched gap where a century of entries should be, and his grandmother's name at the edge of the burn. The stranger dies whispering about 'the garden' and 'the crown that eats.' Emotional beat: grief braided with suspicion—his own family is implicated.

chapters.title: The Thing Wearing the Crown
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the capital, Hazel witnesses the king's procession and sees what no one else can: the crown moves like a jaw, and the king's eyes are full of someone else's memories. Courtiers trade years to the throne for favor. Emotional beat: horror and recognition—the vanished ledger entries feed this.

chapters.title: Ledger of Debts, Ledger of Blood
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. A disgraced guild archivist, Marlow, reveals the Delacroix secret: Hazel's grandmother bound the Verdant to the king to save the guild, paying in her own memories and seeding the debt through the family line. Hazel is not an heir; he is collateral. Emotional beat: betrayal, then grim resolve.

chapters.title: The Road Through Borrowed Country
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel and Marlow travel toward the garden marked on the map, through villages where people have forgotten their own children—places the Verdant has already fed. Hazel begins trading small ledger-memories to help them, feeling each loss like a pulled tooth. Emotional beat: the cost of power made intimate.

chapters.title: The Last Dragon
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, with the dragon Emberlow's POV. In a caldera roost, they find Emberlow, the final dragon, whose fire is the only flame that can unmake the Verdant's roots. Emberlow is dying of memory-hunger too, forgetting her own hoard, her own name. Emotional beat: kinship between two fading keepers.

chapters.title: A Bargain in Ash
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Emberlow agrees to carry them to the garden, but demands a price: Hazel must carry her memories in his ledger, becoming her archive when her fire fails. Marlow warns this is how the Verdant first began—as a bargain freely made. Emotional beat: hope shadowed by foreshadowing.

chapters.title: The Garden That Remembers
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. They reach the garden: a walled paradise where every flower is a stolen memory in bloom, and the air hums with other people's happiest moments. Hazel finds his grandmother's memories growing on a single tree, still alive. Emotional beat: seduction—Hazel wants to stay and read every petal.

chapters.title: Rootwork
chapters.summary: Marlow's POV. Marlow confesses his true role: he was the stranger's partner, sent to retrieve the map, and he has been reporting to the crown. But seeing the garden's roots—vast, pale, threaded through the earth like veins beneath the whole kingdom—turns him. Emotional beat: cowardice cracking into conscience.

chapters.title: The King in the Undercroft
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Guided by the map's deeper layer, they enter the palace undercroft and find the king: old, chained by roots to the Verdant's heart, lucid for the first time in decades. He begs not for freedom but for someone to witness what he did. Emotional beat: pity for a man who sold his kingdom's memory to save it once.

chapters.title: The First Bargain
chapters.summary: The Verdant's POV. Through the king's memories, the story of the Verdant's origin: a famine-era bargain, a guild that promised abundance, and a seedling that learned hunger. The Verdant speaks to Hazel directly, offering to return every memory it holds—including his grandmother's—if he becomes its new keeper. Emotional beat: temptation at its most reasonable.

chapters.title: What Hazel Would Keep
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel nearly accepts, walking the garden's rows and reclaiming fragments of his grandmother's life—her laugh, her ledger-hand, her guilt. Marlow and Emberlow's warnings ring hollow against the smell of growing things. Emotional beat: the quiet corruption of a good intention.

chapters.title: The Guttering
chapters.summary: Emberlow's POV. Emberlow's fire fails catastrophically mid-flight; she crash-lands in the capital's river, half her memories already transferred to Hazel's ledger and burning through him. The crown senses the dragon's weakness and calls the court to a feast of memories. Emotional beat: urgency—the clock is now hours, not days.

chapters.title: Feast of the Faithful
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. At the palace feast, courtiers queue to trade their years to the crown, and Hazel watches a young maid surrender her entire past for her mother's life. Hazel infiltrates the undercroft with Marlow's stolen keys. Emotional beat: righteous anger crystallizing into action.

chapters.title: Unbinding
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. In the undercroft, Hazel begins the unbinding, reading his grandmother's original entries aloud to dissolve the contract's terms. The Verdant fights back with Hazel's own memories, making him relive every loss. The king, freed to his waist, takes up the recitation. Emotional beat: endurance—two voices against a root-system's scream.

chapters.title: The Price of Fire
chapters.summary: Emberlow's POV. Emberlow, dying, crawls to the garden's edge to give her last fire to the roots—but fire needs a living hand to aim it, and she cannot remember how to burn. She gives Hazel her final coherent memory: her first flight, freely given. Emotional beat: sacrifice as inheritance.

chapters.title: Crownfall
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Climax. Hazel carries Emberlow's fire into the garden's heart and learns the truth of free gifts: the memories he has been given, never taken, cannot be consumed by the Verdant. He burns the roots, the crown cracks, and the Verdant—offered, at last, the one thing it never had, a freely given memory—lets go. Emotional beat: terror transfigured into grace.

chapters.title: The King Who Remembered
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. The king, unbound and mortal, remembers his reign's true history and abdicates the memory-trade, ordering the court's debts burned. He asks Hazel to write it all down—not as a ledger of what was taken, but of what was returned. Emotional beat: exhausted, unglamorous repair.

chapters.title: Ash Garden
chapters.summary: Marlow's POV. The garden burns to fertile ash. Marlow, pardoned but unwilling to forget his betrayal, stays to tend the ground where stolen memories are returning to their scattered owners—some joyful reunions, some unbearable. Emotional beat: penance chosen, not imposed.

chapters.title: The New Ledger
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV. Hazel reopens the guildhall with a new first entry: Emberlow's first flight, recorded as a gift. Former debtors arrive, not to trade but to give. Hazel feels his grandmother's memories settling in him like heirlooms rather than wounds. Emotional beat: quiet rebirth of a vocation.

chapters.title: Hazel and the Garden
chapters.summary: Hazel's POV, years later. An old Hazel tends a small garden on the guildhall's roof where the Verdant's last seed, freely planted, grows into something new and harmless—a tree that gives memories back instead of taking. A child asks what the guild does. Emotional beat: the answer, at last, is simple: 'We remember for each other.'
